AGENDA
  GLENDALE ARTS AND CULTURE COMMISSION
  VIA TELECONFERENCE ONLY
 Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
 verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
 glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire devices
 using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings are also
 archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818) 548-4013 for
 program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk's Office.
 If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the
 Library, Arts and Culture Department, at (818) 548-2030, during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
 In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
 language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
 are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
 requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
 to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
 are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM
 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
 Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
 wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
 Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
 the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
 required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  MARCH 17, 2022 AT 2:00 PM

To help slow the transmission of COVID-19, and protect the health and safety of the community, City
Council, as well as Board & Commission meetings, will continue to be closed to the public for in-person
attendance.
The public is encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes to practice social
distancing. Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and
AT&T U-verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire devices
using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu.
For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public comments on a
specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed.

  1. REGULAR BUSINESS AGENDA – 2:00 PM
   Roll Call
  a. Report of Recorder, re: Posting of Agenda. The Agenda for the March 17, 2022
  Regular Meeting of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission was Posted on
  March 14, 2022 on the Bulletin Board Outside City Hall.
2. CONSENT ITEMS (Including Minutes)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the
  Commission or the audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such
  request before motion is proposed.
  a. Minutes of the February 17, 2022 Regular Meeting of the Arts and Culture
  Commission.
  b. Minutes of the March 3, 2022 Special Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission.
3. INTRODUCTIONS AND PRESENTATIONS
  a. Library, Arts & Culture Events – Presented by Jennifer Fukutomi-Jones, Principal

  Arts & Culture Administrator

4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to Items NOT a Part of this Agenda. Each Speaker is Allowed 5 Minutes.
  Members of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission may Question or Respond to the
  Speaker, but there will be no Debate or Decision. The Matter may be Referred to Staff
  Through the Commission Chair for Investigation and Report.
5. ACTION ITEMS
  a. Nomination of one Commissioner to the Artist Review & Selection Committee for

  the Creative Crosswalks RFP.
  1. Motion appointing one Commissioner to the Artist Review & Selection Committee for
  the Creative Crosswalks RFP.
  b. Armenian Genocide Remembrance Monument

  1. Motion recommending to the City Council to approve the acceptance and installation of
  the proposed monument in recognition of the Armenian Genocide, by the Consulate
  General of Armenia, to be located at the Central Library - 222 E. Harvard St.
  c. Cultural Equity and Inclusion Plan – Assessment Report

  1. Motion to Note and File the Cultural Equity and Inclusion Plan – Assessment Report by
  The Aspire Group.
6. DISCUSSION ITEMS
  a. 2021-2022 Work Plan Progress Updates
  1. CITY-WIDE ARTS
  i. Art Happens Anywhere – Projects Update
  ii. LeBasse Projects – Update
  iii. Mural Ordinance – Update
  iv. Storefront Art Program – Update
  2. NEIGHBORHOOD ARTS – No Update
  3. PERFORMING ARTS
   i. 2022 Performance Series – Update
  4. ARTS AND CULTURAL EVENTS – No Update
  5. MARKETING AND COMMUNICATIONS – No Update
7. COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
8. WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS
9. ADJOURNMENT
  The next Regular Meeting of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission is Thursday, April
  21, 2022, at 2:00 P.M. via teleconference only.

CITY OF GLENDALE
  ARTS and CULTURE COMMISSION
  Minutes of Regular Meeting

  Thursday, March 17, 2022 at 2:00 p.m.
1.  ROLL CALL
  •  The meeting was called to order on March 17, 2022 at 2:00 p.m.
  •  Present: Commissioner Vidor, Tufenkian, Zadorian, Vice Chair Viar, Chairperson Yank
  •  The Agenda for the March 17, 2022 Regular Meeting was posted on March 11, 2022 on the Bulletin
  Board outside City Hall.

 2. CONSENT ITEMS (INCLUDING MINUTES)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the Commission or the
  audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such request before motion is proposed.

  a. Minutes of the February 17, 2022 Regular Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission.

  Moved:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Seconded: Commissioner Vidor

  Ayes:  Commissioners Vidor, Tufenkian, Zadorian, Vice Chair Viar, Chairperson Yank
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  None

  b. Minutes of the March 3, 2022 Special Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission.

  Moved:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Seconded: Commissioner Vidor

  Ayes:  Commissioners Vidor, Tufenkian, Zadorian, Vice Chair Viar, Chairperson Yank
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  None

3. INTRODUCTIONS & PRESENTATIONS
  a. Library, Arts & Culture Events – Presented by Jennifer Fukutomi-Jones, Principal Arts & Culture
  Administrator

 4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to Items NOT a Part of this Agenda. Each Speaker is Allowed 5 Minutes. Members of
  the Arts and Culture Commission may Question or Respond to the Speaker, but there will be no Debate or
  Decision. The Matter may be Referred to Staff Through the Commission Chair for Investigation and Report.
  – No Speakers

  1
 5. ACTION ITEM(s)
  a. Nomination of one Commissioner to the Artist Review & Selection Committee for the Creative
  Crosswalks RFP.
  1. Motion appointing one Commissioner to the Artist Review & Selection Committee for the Creative
  Crosswalks RFP.
  • The Commission asked questions and gave their feedback.

  Moved:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Seconded: Commissioner Vidor

  That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby appoints Commissioner Yank to the Artist Review &
  Selection Committee for the Creative Crosswalks RFP, as more fully outlined in the March 17, 2022
  Report by the Library, Arts & Culture’s Principal Arts & Culture Administrator.

  Ayes:  Commissioners Vidor, Tufenkian, Zadorian, Vice Chair Viar, Chairperson Yank
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  None

  b. Armenian Genocide Remembrance Monument
  1. Motion recommending to the City Council to approve the acceptance and installation of the
  proposed monument in recognition of the Armenian Genocide, by the Consulate General of
  Armenia, to be located at the Central Library - 222 E. Harvard St.

  • The Commission asked questions and gave their feedback.

  Moved:  Commissioner Vidor
  Seconded: Commissioner Tufenkian

  That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby recommends that the City Council approve the
  acceptance and installation of the proposed monument in recognition of the Armenian Genocide, by
  the Consulate General of Armenia, to be located at the Central Library - 222 E. Harvard St., as
  more fully outlined in the March 17, 2022 Report by the Library, Arts & Culture’s Principal Arts &
  Culture Administrator.

  Ayes:  Commissioners Vidor, Tufenkian, Zadorian, Vice Chair Viar, Chairperson Yank
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  None

  c. Cultural Equity and Inclusion Plan – Assessment Report
  1. Motion to Note and File the Cultural Equity and Inclusion Plan – Assessment Report by The Aspire
  Group.
  • The Commission asked questions and gave their feedback.
  Moved:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Seconded: Commissioner Vidor

  2
   That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby receives, notes and files the Cultural Equity and
  inclusion Plan – Assessment Report by The Aspire Group, as more fully outlined in the March 17,
  2022 Report by the Library, Arts & Culture’s Principal Arts & Culture Administrator.

  Ayes:  Commissioners Vidor, Tufenkian, Zadorian, Vice Chair Viar, Chairperson Yank
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  None

6. DISCUSSION ITEM(s) / REPORT(s)
  a. 2021-2022 Work Plan Progress Updates
  1. CITY-WIDE ARTS
  i. Art Happens Anywhere (AHA)– Projects Update
  • Ms. Fukutomi Jones gave a brief update on Impending Storms currently on display and
  upcoming music event happening in April.

  ii. LeBasse Projects – Update
  • Ms. Fukutomi Jones gave a brief update on the LeBasse RFQ progress.

  iii. Mural Ordinance – Update
  • Ms. Fukutomi Jones stated that staff is working diligently to have a Mural Ordinance draft
  ready for review at the April Commission meeting.

  iv. Storefront Art Program – Update
  • Ms. Fukutomi Jones gave a brief update and stated staff has released an application
  process and request for artists and it will be ongoing.

  2. NEIGHBORHOOD ARTS – No Update

  3. PERFORMING ARTS
  i. 2022 Performance Series – Update
  • Ms. Fukutomi Jones gave a brief update on the programming recommendations for the
  upcoming 2022 series and shared the passing of Barbara Morrison, who staff thanked and
  honored as a well-respected and loved Jazz musician who performed at the Brand Library
  Summer Series many times.

  4. ARTS AND CULTURAL EVENTS – No Update

  5. MARKETING AND COMMUNICATIONS – No Update

7. COMMISSION / STAFF COMMENTS
  •  The Commission thanked Staff for their work.
  •  Regarding the proposed Creative Crosswalk and Intersection Asphalt Murals Request for
  Proposals (RFP), Commissioner Vidor gave feedback on the color choices described in the
  RFP and recommended including more vibrant colors; Commissioner Zadorian agreed with
  Commissioner Vidor’s comment; and Commissioner Yank gave her input. Sarkis
  Oganesyan, Principal Civil Engineer/Acting City Engineer for the Public Works Department,
  is aware of the recommendations, concerns and feedback, and is flexible working with
  Commission.
  •  Dr. Shaffer stated he would like Commission to close the meeting in honor of Barbara
  Morrison.

  3
 8. WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS- Three written communications received and forwarded to Commission.

9. ADJOURNMENT
The next Regular Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission is April 21, 2022, at 2:00 p.m., in City Council
Chambers (2nd Floor), 613 E. Broadway.
